Anya (Docs): Hey team — quick alignment ask. I'm putting together a short docs style guidance PR about voice + product naming. Need input on a few points before I open the PR: 1) preferred tone (neutral, engineering-forward, or customer-facing?), 2) canonical product names to use in copy (use full product names vs short forms), 3) a few glossary entries that feel ambiguous (serving runtime, dedicated/reserved, private). Can folks weigh in? :wave:
Sam (Eng): +1 on an engineering-forward tone but readable. Keep examples concise. For product names I think we should prefer the branded names from marketing (Redwood API / Redwood Dedicated / Redwood Private) on first mention, then short forms (API / Dedicated / Private) afterwards.
Kai (Product): Agree with Sam. Use the branded names first. For tone: neutral + pragmatic — don't oversell capabilities, but call out tradeoffs (latency/cost).
George (Research): For glossary, can we add a short note that "serving runtime" = the inference engine + kernel selection + KV cache behavior? One sentence plus links to infra docs is enough.
Anya (Docs): Perfect. Here's my proposed canonical phrasing for the glossary (draft):
```
Serving runtime — The GPU-optimized inference engine that executes model requests, manages the KV cache, and selects optimized kernels based on model and workload characteristics. See /eng-runtime for low-level details.
```
Anya (Docs): Also proposing we standardize on these naming rules in docs: *First mention*: use full product name (Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console, Redwood Optimize). *Subsequent mentions*: short form (API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize). Avoid generic terms like "reserved capacity" unless quoting product UX.
Sam (Eng): That naming rule works. One note: some internal repos still refer to "reserved" — we should add a migration checklist to PR to search/replace common variants (reserved, dedicated capacity, dedicated pool). I can run a grep and post a short list.
Emma (Docs): I can take editorial pass after PR is opened. Also let's include a small guidance section for SDK snippets: prefer using the official SDK naming (redwood.client.generate / redwood.client.embed) instead of ad-hoc examples. Example snippet to include in the PR:
```javascript
// Preferred JS snippet style
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Summarize the doc' });
```
Kai (Product): Nice. Can we add a one-liner for "Private" so support/enterprise teams know it covers VPC and on-prem? e.g., "Redwood Private — customer-managed control plane for VPC or on-prem deployments."
Anya (Docs): Yep adding that to glossary. Also proposing we add a quick migration checklist in the PR description: - search/replace deprecated terms - update examples to branded SDK calls - fix internal links to /eng-runtime and /deployments - add one-liner definitions for product page tooltips
Sam (Eng): I'll run the search now and paste results into the PR comments. Expect a follow-up in ~30m.
doc-bot: New PR opened by Anya (Docs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 — "docs: style guide + naming glossary"
Anya (Docs): @Emma can you review when you have a sec? @Kai @Sam tagging for technical review. I'll include a tiny eval checklist to make sure wording doesn't affect tests that assert exact strings in some guides.
Emma (Docs): On it. Plan to review tomorrow morning. If anyone has language they'd like to preserve for marketing copy, flag it now so I don't rewrite it out.
George (Research): Quick note — for the "serving runtime" glossary entry please include a parenthetical about "latency vs throughput tradeoffs" so it's clear why batching/kv-caching matter.
Anya (Docs): Good call. Final draft I'll add: "(includes batching and KV caching behavior that trade off latency and throughput)."
Sam (Eng): FYI I found three internal docs using "reserved capacity" and two examples calling it "dedicated pool" — I'll paste links in the PR comment.
Anya (Docs): Thanks Sam. If anyone else sees other variants, drop them in PR comments. Goal: small, surgical edits, no major content changes. We'll ship as an atomic docs-only PR. :rocket:
Kai (Product): Sounds good. Approving the approach.
Anya (Docs): Closing thread — will iterate in PR. Thanks all! :sparkles:
